The server is already live. What is still offline is the Grok side, and Cursor cannot finish that from this repo.

[https://waypoint-5o4r.onrender.com/healthz](https://waypoint-5o4r.onrender.com/healthz) answers `ok (database on, data is kept, texts on)`. That Render service already has a public HTTPS address, Redis, and Twilio. `WAYPOINT_PUBLIC_URL` is optional here: the server uses Render’s own `RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL` when that variable is unset. The local `data/store.json` and empty `accounts.json` only describe this machine. They are not the live database.

**Still required, in this order**

1. On the live site, create an account (the demo does not hand out a Bot key). Open **Connect your Bots** and copy the connector. It will be `https://waypoint-5o4r.onrender.com/mcp` plus `Authorization: Bearer <that account’s key>`.
2. In Grok, add a custom MCP server named Waypoint with that URL and header, then list its tools.
3. Create the five Bots and paste each brief from that same Connect page. Only the Manager gets a schedule: 2:00 AM. The four workers stay on call.
4. Tell the Manager to create the webhook routine named “Waypoint check now” (the Connect page has that message ready to copy). Paste the URL and key it returns into Waypoint Settings. Until that webhook is saved, **Check now** still writes a simulated Case Clerk and Manager run and does not wake Grok.
5. Put a real phone number on the account. Texting is switched on at the host. The sample people use `555` numbers, so their texts are not delivered unless `SMS_DEMO_TO` is set.

Intake Clerk stays chat-only. There is no server piece to deploy for it.

**What Cursor cannot do.** Grok Bot has no API in this session. The MCP server, the five briefs, the 2:00 AM routine, and the webhook are created in Grok while you are signed in. I can walk the live site and the Connect page with you in the browser once you are logged into both Waypoint and Grok.

<timestamp>Thursday, Nov 19, 2026, 3:55 PM (UTC-8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
can we not connect the bots on the backend for all users?
</user_query>

Each person needs their own Grok Bots. One backend connection cannot serve every account.

A Bot key is the account boundary. The master key on the server only sees the sample people, the profiles with no owner. A signed-in account’s key only sees that account’s profile. `list_people`, `get_brief`, and every write check that set and refuse anyone else. Putting one key in a shared Grok connector therefore reaches one account, or the demo, and nothing more.

The wake-up path is per person too. **Check now** calls the webhook saved on that profile. A single Manager routine has one webhook, so it can be the wake-up for only the profile you paste it onto.

Messenger also runs inside that person’s Grok account. Calendar events and Gmail drafts use the Google account connected to those Bots. A Bot logged in as you would write to your calendar and your drafts, then text your phone.

The shared part is already on the server: one public `/mcp` address, the deadline math, the store, and Twilio. What each person pastes in is their own key, their five briefs, and their Manager webhook.
